summary: Replace ShipRight's hand-built sign-in (own JWT, refresh tokens, password reset, Company/User tables, IsAdmin flag) with ASP.NET Core Identity backed by the existing SQL/Dapper-style data access (no EF Core), add roles, Google sign-in, and per-company (tenant) scoping of users, logins and roles. Still open: what happens to existing accounts and passwords.

ask.text: People already have ShipRight accounts with passwords. When the new sign-in system goes live, should those people still be able to log in with their current email and password?
ask.why: It decides whether existing accounts, passwords and company data are carried over (needs a migration and a way to read the old password format) or whether everyone starts from scratch.

options.label: Yes, keep existing accounts and passwords working
options.consequence: Existing users and companies are migrated; nobody has to re-register or reset a password. More careful migration work and tests.

options.label: Keep accounts, but everyone must reset their password once
options.consequence: Accounts and companies are kept, old passwords are discarded; each person gets a reset email on first use.

options.label: No, start fresh
options.consequence: Existing accounts are not carried over; everyone registers again. Simplest, but existing data tied to a company is lost or orphaned.

coverage.note: Existing-account migration, roles and how tenants are identified still to confirm.
Depends on migration answer; existing Company/User tables use CompanyId.
Which role may do what; currently only IsAdmin exists.
Password rules and messages to confirm.
Login/register/Google screens already exist in front-end; changes depend on answers.
Same email in two companies allowed or not.
Users per company and paging for any user/role list.
Email and Google profile data stored.
Security expectations (lockout, token lifetime) to confirm.
